items.title: Indiana Monthly Water Resource Summary — September 2026
items.summary: Precipitation: During September 2026, Indiana’s average precipitation was slightly below normal, with a statewide monthly precipitation average of 91 percent normal. Drought Monitor: For October 6, 2026, the U.S. Drought Monitor shows most of the far southern portions of Indiana experiencing “abnormally dry” conditions and no drought conditions for the rest of Indiana. The U.S. Seasonal Drought Outlook predicts no drought conditions through at least the end of December 2026. Streamflow: In September 2026, ten of the twelve streams included in drought reporting since 1999 had above normal to significantly above normal stream flow. Muscatatuck River near Deputy had the lowest mean monthly flow at 16%, and the St. Groundwater: As of September 30, 2026, new water level data is available for all nine wells currently monitored. Data indicates that water level is above normal for four of the nine wells: Laporte 9, Fulton 7, Vigo 7, and Morgan 4. Data indicates that the water level is near normal for Randolph 3, Posey 3, and Harrison 8; and water level remains well below normal for LaGrange 2 and Clark 20.
